init.welcomeDesc: Git identities and encrypted private keys stay on this device. Choose how to start:
init.createDesc: First-time setup. Create a local access password and recovery key.
init.createDescMobile: Brand new setup. Create an encrypted database, access password, and offline recovery key.
init.restoreDesc: You already have another device. Enter cloud storage and that device’s recovery key.
init.restoreDescMobile: The computer must already be synced to the cloud. Scan the QR to write cloud settings, then enter the recovery key.
init.restoreDescMobilePick: Already have data on a computer? Scan the QR to import cloud settings, then enter the old recovery key.
init.chooseDesc: Create a workspace if this is a new setup. Restore from the cloud with the other device’s recovery key if you already have data.

titles.oldRecovery: Enter the old device recovery key

descs.create0: Keys and config files are encrypted in your local folder and never uploaded in plaintext.
descs.create1: This password unlocks the app on this device. If you forget it, only the recovery key can reset access.
descs.create2: The recovery key is shown once. It is the only way to recover a new machine or a forgotten password. Store it offline.
descs.create3: Paste the recovery key you just saved to confirm you actually wrote it down.
descs.create4: The encrypted workspace is ready. You can start using the app.
descs.restore0: Restored identities and keys will be written into this local folder. Choose an empty folder that is not initialized.
descs.restore1: Enter the exact same R2 / S3 connection details (including prefix) as the old device.
descs.restore2: Enter the recovery key saved when the old device was initialized, to decrypt cloud data.
descs.restore3: Set a daily access password for this device. It can differ from the old one. The old recovery key stays valid.
descs.restore4: The workspace was rebuilt with the same master key. Both devices can keep syncing.

settings.title: Settings
settings.desc: Workspace security, app preferences, and account settings

language.title: Interface language
language.hint: Changes apply immediately — no restart. Start menu / Dock names follow the installer language and will not change here. A few backend errors may still be in Chinese in this release.

settings.notesAutoSaveTip: When on, the note is encrypted and saved when the pointer or focus leaves the Markdown editor. When off, it only saves if you click Save or confirm leaving with unsaved changes.
settings.notesAutoSaveHint: Title, group, and tags still need Save unless you later leave the body editor. Auto-save only runs on leaving the Markdown pane.
settings.appCardDesc: End-to-end encrypted vault and credential hub
settings.backgroundRunTip: When on, the system Back key on the home screen returns to the phone home without killing the app. When off, Back quits the app.
settings.backgroundRunOn: Background run is on. Back on the home screen returns to the system home.
settings.backgroundRunOff: Background run is off. Back on the home screen quits the app.
settings.unlockAnimHint: Play a visual transition after a successful password unlock
settings.unlockAnimTip: Plays after you unlock with a password or recovery key. Silent grace unlocks do not trigger it.
settings.unlockAnimHintDesktop: When off, unlock goes straight to the main screen. Click or press Esc / Space / Enter to skip.
settings.launchTip: Open this app after you sign in. Windows uses the current-user Startup item; macOS uses Login Items. If grace unlock is on, keys may be loaded into ssh-agent.
settings.launchUnsupported: Launch at login is not supported on this system.
settings.launchHint: Example: turn this on after reinstalling on a travel laptop. Off by default.
settings.closeActionTip: What happens when you click the window close button.
settings.closeCurrent: Current: {{action}}. You can check “Remember my choice” in the confirmation. Reopening from the tray follows the grace-day setting.
settings.pwMin: New password must be at least 8 characters
settings.pwMismatch: The two new passwords do not match
settings.graceRange: Grace days must be between 0 and 30
settings.graceOff: Grace unlock disabled. The next launch needs the access password.
settings.graceOn: Grace unlock set for {{days}} day(s) after sign-in
settings.closeReset: Close action reset to ask every time
settings.graceTip: 0 means the access password is required every launch. 1–30 remembers unlock on this PC via Windows DPAPI and loads the agent. After expiry you must enter the password again. Switching Windows users or changing the Windows password invalidates it.
settings.graceHint: Example: 7 means a week without the password; 0 means always verify.
settings.graceValidUntil: Skip-unlock is valid until {{when}}. After that the access password is required.
settings.gracePending: Days without password are set, but this session is not active or has expired. It applies again after the next password unlock.
settings.bioIntro: Uses Windows Hello / Touch ID already enrolled on this device. This app never collects or stores fingerprints. Enabling requires the access password.
settings.bioUnavailable: No fingerprint, face, or Windows Hello hardware detected.
settings.bioStale: The biometric credential is stale. Unlock with the access password, then enable again.
settings.bioEnableTip: Unlock the workspace with the system fingerprint. Password and recovery key always remain as fallback.
settings.bioPasswordPh: Enter the access password to enable
settings.bioEnabledHint: On. Unlock and reveal codes/passwords can use the system fingerprint.
settings.bioReveal: Allow fingerprint when viewing codes / passwords
settings.bioRevealTip: After the vault is unlocked, viewing a one-time code or account password can use fingerprint instead of the access password.
settings.bioRevealDefault: On by default with the main switch
settings.bioExport: Also allow fingerprint to reveal TOTP secrets
settings.bioExportTip: This is an export-level action. The access password is required by default.
settings.screenshotAllowTip: Off by default so codes and secrets are not captured by system screenshots, recordings, or some screen-sharing tools. Turn on only to back up a QR code or show the UI to support.
settings.screenshotAllowHint: When on, this app can be captured; turning it off restores protection immediately
settings.screenshotHintExclude: By default, system screenshots, recordings, and some screen-sharing tools cannot capture this window (you may see a black frame). Turn on to capture QR codes or share the UI.
settings.screenshotHintOverlay: iOS does not let apps fully block screenshots. When this is off, the app hides its contents in the app switcher. The system may still allow a screenshot.
settings.screenshotHintUnsupported: This system cannot intercept screenshots. The switch is remembered, but local captures can still include this window.
settings.screenshotOn: Screenshots are allowed. This window can be captured.
settings.screenshotOff: Screenshots are blocked again where the system supports it.
settings.screenshotTaken: A system screenshot was taken. This OS cannot fully block capture — make sure nobody nearby can see codes.
settings.revealTitle: Grace period for viewing OTP / passwords
settings.revealIntro: Independent of startup skip-unlock. Ends immediately on lock or quit. Revealing a TOTP secret still always requires the password.
settings.revealGraceTip: After the first verification, viewing codes or passwords again within this window does not re-prompt. 0 means every time.
settings.clipWatchTip: Off by default. When on, only Git repo URLs are recognized and a light hint is shown. Anything else is discarded immediately and never logged.
settings.clipWatchHint: The clipboard is not read while locked. Turn this on only on a trusted machine.
settings.clipWatchOn: On — copied Git URLs suggest a clone
settings.rotateIntro: Generate a new recovery key and retire the old one. Save it immediately.
settings.wsSleepLockHint: Controlled by the local lockOnSleep setting. See the security checklist.
settings.backupIntro: Offline encrypted backup (.gambackup) and restore, plus end-to-end zero-knowledge sync to S3 / Cloudflare R2.
settings.patTokenPh: Paste the PAT for the selected host
settings.bioIntroMobile: Unlock with the access password, or switch to a fingerprint already enrolled on this device. The recovery key always works as a fallback.
settings.bioMethodTip: Fingerprint must already be enrolled, and bound once with the access password.
settings.bioUnavailableMobile: This device has no usable fingerprint. Use the access password.
settings.clipClearTip: Clears copied secrets so other apps are less likely to read them from the clipboard.
settings.histLimitTip: How many previous passwords to keep when you change one.

proxy.title: Network proxy
proxy.enableTip: Applies only to requests from this app (updates, GitHub API, Git HTTPS, SSH, cloud sync). Does not change the system proxy.
proxy.hint: Turn on if GitHub / GitLab is unstable in your region. The password is stored in the local config file.
proxy.gitHttpsTip: Writes HTTP(S)_PROXY when this app runs git clone over HTTPS.
proxy.sshTip: Injects ProxyCommand for ssh / git launched by this app. Needs Git’s connect or ncat. Does not edit ~/.ssh/config.
proxy.cloudTip: R2 / S3 backups follow the master switch. Turn this off for domestic object storage.
proxy.httpsFail: GitHub HTTPS failed. Check the proxy.

security.intro1: This list only reads local config and the workspace path. Everything is computed on this device. No telemetry.
security.intro2: The OS will not tell this app who is watching the clipboard or capturing the screen, so we cannot name a listener.
security.intro3: Clipboard exclusion is a cooperative hint for history, cloud clipboards, and well-behaved managers. Malware can ignore it. It does not stop trojans or black out screenshots.
security.noTodos: Nothing pending. Passed checks are collapsed below.

factory.warn: This clears workspace data, restores the ~/.ssh entry, undoes user env / Git / terminal hooks written by this app, and deletes local config. Cloud data is not deleted. This cannot be undone.
factory.reconfirm: Type 清空 below, then run the reset. The confirmation word is always 清空.

cardHint.github: Used to upload public keys and import organizations. See the guide for the scopes to check.
cardHint.gitlab: Used to upload public keys and import groups. See the guide for the scopes to check.
cardHint.gitee: Used to upload public keys and import organizations. See the guide for the scopes to check.

pat.guideNote: The token is stored in the vault and never shown again here. It is verified immediately after save.

github.intro: In GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens → Tokens (classic), choose Generate new token (classic). Do not use Fine-grained.
scopes: write:public_key — add SSH public keys to the account
extra: repo — create Releases on private and public repos
public_repo — enough if you only publish public repos

gitlab.intro: Create a token in GitLab → Preferences → Access Tokens.
scopes: api — read account/groups, upload SSH keys; also covers publishing Releases

gitee.intro: Create a token in Gitee → Settings → Private tokens.

pat.reauthHint: Viewing or copying the token requires the workspace access password.

tokenTip.github: Open the setup guide to see which GitHub classic scopes to check.
tokenTip.gitlab: Open the setup guide to see which GitLab scopes to check.
tokenTip.gitee: Open the setup guide to see which Gitee scopes to check.

ghCli.title: GitHub CLI
ghCli.hint: Sign the local gh CLI in so the terminal and Cursor can publish Releases. This opens GitHub’s device login page; the one-time code appears here and in the console. gh keeps the token; it is not stored here.
ghCli.deviceCode: Enter this code in the 8 boxes on GitHub
ghCli.pasteCode: The code is copied. Paste it in the browser, click Continue, and this page will show Signed in.
ghCli.noCode: No code yet. Check the one-time code line in the console window, or sign in again.
ghCli.ok: Signed in to GitHub CLI as {{name}}

pages.overviewDesc: Keys, SSH config, agent, and connectivity for every Git identity
pages.totpDesc: Codes stay masked until you reveal them. Switch between cards and a list.
pages.accountsDesc: Group multiple logins per site. Passwords and linked 2FA stay masked.
pages.filesDesc: Encrypt IDs, key backups, and attachments. Zero-knowledge cloud sync.
pages.notesDesc: Private Markdown notes with encrypted images and lossless compression.
pages.syncDesc: Pulls once at startup, then follows the schedule and local edits. Opening this page does not probe the cloud again.
pages.noIdentities: No Git identities yet. Create them on a computer, then sync to this phone.

syncPage.wifiOnlyHint: On cellular, sync identities, accounts, and note text only. Large files wait for Wi-Fi or a manual push.
syncPage.attachmentsManualHint: Scheduled and startup sync skip files and note images. Transfer them only on manual push/pull.
syncPage.importCfgOk: ✅ Imported S3/R2 config. Review and save.
syncPage.shareNeedCfg: ❌ Fill in cloud storage first, then share a QR code
syncPage.shareOk: ✅ QR code ready. It has connection info only — no recovery key, and it does not push data.
syncPage.scanHint: Point at a QR code from another device’s Share config
syncPage.scanNone: ❌ That QR code isn’t a cloud-storage config
syncPage.scanOk: ✅ Cloud storage written. The QR code has no recovery key; restoring still needs the recovery key at setup.
syncPage.testNeed: Fill Endpoint, Bucket, Access Key, and Secret Key first
syncPage.backupPwShort: Backup password must be at least 8 characters
syncPage.backupPwMismatch: The two backup passwords don’t match
syncPage.exportAccessPwHint: A backup holds every private key, account password and 2FA secret, so exporting requires re-entering your access password.
syncPage.confirmPushMsg: This encrypts the current workspace and uploads it.
syncPage.confirmPushDetail: The latest snapshot replaces what’s already in the cloud. Other devices get it on the next pull.
syncPage.confirmPullMsg: This reads the latest encrypted cloud data and merges it here.
syncPage.confirmPullDetail: Local identities, keys, and settings may be overwritten. Confirm this is the device you want.
syncPage.confirmRestoreDetail: This overwrites current identities, keys, and settings. It cannot be undone.
syncPage.statusHint: This is the last startup or auto-sync result. Click Refresh to check the cloud now. Data is encrypted before it leaves the device.
syncPage.periodHint: Startup pulls once. Then it pulls then pushes on a schedule. Editing an identity or key pushes immediately.
syncPage.guideHint: No cloud account yet? Use the beginner guide to create a bucket and two keys, then fill this page. Cloudflare R2 is the easiest start.
syncPage.endpointTip: The S3 API URL from your provider. Must start with https:// or http://. Don’t paste a console webpage.
syncPage.bucketTip: The exact bucket name from the console. Lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only. Keep it private.
syncPage.regionTip: Use auto for R2. For AWS, match the bucket region. MinIO is usually us-east-1.
syncPage.prefixTip: A folder inside the bucket. Default gam-sync/. Other devices must use the same prefix.
syncPage.akTip: The access key from your provider, not your login email.
syncPage.skTip: The secret shown only once when the key is created. Don’t send it in chat or email.
syncPage.exportCfgAccessPwHint: The file includes the Secret Access Key, which can control the bucket. Being unlocked is not enough — re-enter your access password.
syncPage.revealKeysHint: Reveal the Access Key and Secret Key only after verifying this vault’s access password.
syncPage.shareCfgReauthHint: The QR code includes the Access Key and Secret Key, which can control the bucket. Re-enter your access password before sharing.
syncPage.snapsHint: Keeps the last 10 snapshots and a daily copy for 14 days. You can roll back on demand.
syncPage.noSnaps: No snapshots yet. They appear after the first push.
syncPage.e2eeNote: Zero-knowledge encryption: assets are encrypted locally with XChaCha20-Poly1305. Cloud names are HMAC-hashed. The provider cannot read them.
syncPage.exportHint: Packs identities, keys, and repo private keys into one encrypted file for cold backup or moving machines.
syncPage.importHint: Restore from a .gambackup file. You can preview the inventory before merging.
syncPage.importOk: ✅ Backup imported. Workspace merged ({{identities}} identities, {{keys}} keys).
syncPage.shareNote: The QR code has connection info only — no recovery key, and it does not push data. Push first if the phone needs the latest vault. Restoring still needs the recovery key.

agent.misalignWin2: Applying the current Git agent to this machine is your choice. Nothing is changed automatically.
agent.misalignUnix1: The terminal and git are not fully wired to the ssh-agent started by this app.
agent.misalignUnix2: New terminals pick up the same environment only after the startup script is hooked. Applying it is your choice; nothing is changed automatically.

s3guide.title: Cloud storage beginner guide
s3guide.btnTip: Step-by-step: create a bucket and get keys
s3guide.intro: This app will not create a cloud account for you. First prepare a bucket and two keys (Access Key / Secret Key) at the provider, then fill the form. Data is encrypted on this device before upload; the provider cannot read it.
s3guide.keepKeys: Keep both keys private. Don’t send them in chat or email. When restoring on another computer, all 6 fields must match the old device (including the prefix).
s3guide.afterFill: Then go back to the form, save, and test the connection.
s3guide.r2Blurb: Cloudflare R2 is like a drive. Personal backup usually stays in the free tier. Signup may ask for a card, but light use rarely bills. Finish each step before the next.
s3guide.r2s1t: Sign up and sign in to Cloudflare
s3guide.r2s1b: Open Cloudflare, register with email, and sign in. If you already have an account, just sign in.
s3guide.r2s2b: In the console sidebar find Storage & Databases, or search R2. Open the R2 overview. First use may ask you to enable R2.
s3guide.r2s3b: Click Create bucket. Use lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens, e.g. git-keymaster-backup. Location can stay Automatic. Keep it private. Remember the name — that is the Bucket in this app.
s3guide.r2s4b: Back on the R2 overview, open Manage API tokens. Create an API token. Permission: Object Read & Write. Limit it to that bucket if you can.
s3guide.r2s5b: The page shows Access Key ID, Secret Access Key, and Endpoint (https://….r2.cloudflarestorage.com). The secret is shown once. Copy it to a notes file. The account ID is also on the R2 overview if you need to build the endpoint.
s3guide.r2s6b: Endpoint is the full URL (include https://). Bucket is the name. Region is auto. Prefix should stay gam-sync/ and must match on every computer. Fill Access Key ID and Secret Access Key. Save, then test the connection.
s3guide.r2f2: Bucket = the name you just created
s3guide.s3Blurb: AWS S3 is Amazon object storage. Signup usually needs an international card and is usage-billed. A small encrypted backup pack is cheap. Don’t use root-account keys.
s3guide.s3s1t: Sign up and sign in to AWS
s3guide.s3s1b: Open the AWS console and register. Verify email, phone, and payment. Note the region in the top-right, e.g. Singapore ap-southeast-1, Tokyo ap-northeast-1, US East us-east-1.
s3guide.s3s2b: Search S3. Create bucket. Names are globally unique — lowercase and hyphens, e.g. git-keymaster-backup-your-initials. Pick a nearby region and remember it. Block all public access. Other options can stay default.
s3guide.s3s3t: Create an IAM user for this bucket only
s3guide.s3s3b: Don’t use your login password as a key. IAM → Users → Create user, e.g. git-keymaster-sync. Then Security credentials → Create access key. Use “Third-party application” or “Local code”.
s3guide.s3s4b: On the user’s Permissions tab, attach a policy. Beginners can use AmazonS3FullAccess; safer is only this bucket’s s3:ListBucket / GetObject / PutObject / DeleteObject. Without permission, the connection test fails.
s3guide.s3s5b: Copy Access Key ID (usually starts with AKIA) and Secret Access Key immediately. The secret is shown once.
s3guide.s3s6b: Endpoint is https://s3.REGION.amazonaws.com, e.g. https://s3.ap-southeast-1.amazonaws.com. Region is the same code. Bucket is the name. Prefix gam-sync/. Save and test.
s3guide.s3f2: Bucket = the name you just created
s3guide.s3f3: Region = the bucket region, e.g. ap-southeast-1
s3guide.minioBlurb: MinIO is S3-compatible storage on your PC or LAN. Use it if you don’t want backups on a public cloud. You must start MinIO yourself.
s3guide.minios1b: Download MinIO for your OS and start it from the docs. Default console is http://127.0.0.1:9001; S3 API is http://127.0.0.1:9000. The first start prints or asks for a login.
s3guide.minios2t: Sign in and create a bucket
s3guide.minios2b: Open the console, sign in, Create Bucket. Lowercase and hyphens. Don’t make it public.
s3guide.minios3b: Create keys under Access Keys, or use the root username as Access Key ID and the password as Secret Access Key (only on a personal test box).
s3guide.minios4b: Local MinIO endpoint is usually http://127.0.0.1:9000. On another machine, use that IP or hostname plus port. Region is us-east-1 (MinIO often ignores it, but this app needs a value). Bucket is the name; prefix gam-sync/.
s3guide.miniof2: Bucket = the name from the console
s3guide.otherBlurb: Aliyun OSS, Tencent COS, UPYUN, and many others work if they offer an S3-compatible API. The fields may be named AccessKey, SecretKey, Endpoint, Bucket.
s3guide.others1b: In the provider console, confirm the docs say Amazon S3 API. Some products have a separate “S3 compatible” switch.
s3guide.others2b: Create a private bucket. Note the name and region (e.g. oss-cn-hangzhou, ap-guangzhou).
s3guide.others3t: Create a sub-user key, not the root account
s3guide.others3b: In IAM / CAM / RAM, create a user that can only access this bucket, then create an AccessKey. Root keys are riskier if leaked.
s3guide.others4t: Copy the Endpoint from the docs
s3guide.others4b: It must be an S3 API URL, usually https://, sometimes with a region, e.g. https://oss-cn-hangzhou.aliyuncs.com. Don’t paste a console webpage or a custom domain unless the docs say it speaks S3.
s3guide.others5b: Endpoint = the provider’s S3 Endpoint. Bucket = the name. Region = the documented region (try auto first). Prefix gam-sync/. Save and test.
s3guide.otherf1: Endpoint = S3 Endpoint from the docs
s3guide.otherf3: Region = documented region, or try auto
